Anyone who can push to an image name in a registry can point an existing tag at another image; a digest always names the same image.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs Concepts > Containers > Images ('Tags can be moved to point to different images, but digests are fixed')

claims.text: When an image reference contains both a tag and a digest, Kubernetes uses only the digest for pulling.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs Concepts > Containers > Images, image names list: 'Image name with tag and digest. Only the digest will be used for pulling.'

claims.text: Argo CD 3.1 has no image signature verification: it applies the manifests in Git as written, whatever image they name (its GnuPG feature verifies Git commits, not images).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs (argo-cd.readthedocs.io) User Guide > GnuPG verification (commit signatures only); absence of image signature verification in Argo CD 3.1 docs

claims.text: Refusing unverified images for every Pod needs a check in the cluster at Pod creation; devops/supply-chain installs none. k8s.l3.admission-policies later requires a digest at admission, but signatures are still checked only on the commit path.
claims.source_hint: DECISIONS.md §3 2026-10-06 outline devops/supply-chain decision (3); content/tracks/k8s/track.yaml k8s.l3.admission-policies
